university: The University of Texas Medical Branch at Galveston

documents.unit: UTMB Legal Affairs, Compliance, Information Security, Information Services
documents.title: UTMB Artificial Intelligence (AI) Joint Policy
documents.stance_why: The document says students "must abide by AI policies or statements for the UTMB schools and courses" and that faculty are "strongly encouraged to develop their own policies ... allowing or disallowing some or all uses", so it sets no default stance for coursework and hands the decision to instructors; the fixed prohibitions concern confidential data, not course AI use.
documents.summary: UTMB's joint policy from Legal Affairs, Compliance, Information Security and Information Services adapts UT Austin language. It leaves AI rules for coursework to schools and instructors, with a fallback that treats uncited AI like outside help, and focuses on data-privacy limits, student responsibility, citation, and discipline.

units.why: The opening sentence states the institution's direction for generative AI ("actively expanding its use ... to meet the evolving needs of the workforce"), a framing preamble, so P56; it sets no rule, hence informs and neutral.
units.anchor: UTMB is actively expanding its use of Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools

units.why: The sentence says the UT Austin acceptable-use language was adopted "with some modifications"; it describes how the guidance was made, so P84 rather than P56.
units.anchor: we have included their language on this webpage with some modifications
units.policy: UTMB included the University of Texas at Austin language on acceptable use of ChatGPT and Similar AI Tools on this webpage with some modifications.

units.why: "Subject to change" says the guidance is provisional, which is P54 (revisit policy).
units.anchor: Information displayed on this website is subject to change

units.why: Faculty and staff are told to "continually check this website for the latest policy information", a duty to stay current, so P102 rather than P54 (which is about the policy being revised).
units.anchor: continually check this website for the latest policy information and guidance

units.why: The background names benefits ("promote learning, innovation, and creativity and enhance educational experiences") of generative AI without a rule or career claim, so P87.
units.anchor: potential benefits of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies to promote learning, innovation, and creativity

units.why: Students "must abide by AI policies or statements for the UTMB schools and courses" in which they are enrolled, so the student must learn and follow the applicable AI rules, P78; the school-level mention (P85) is secondary.
units.anchor: students must abide by AI policies or statements for the UTMB schools and courses
units.fit_note: Also says schools as well as courses may have AI policies (P85).

units.why: Faculty are "strongly encouraged to develop their own policies ... including allowing or disallowing some or all uses", so the decision is left to each instructor, P04; no university-wide default is set.
units.anchor: Faculty are strongly encouraged to develop their own policies regulating the use of generative AI

units.why: "These policies should be clearly defined in the course syllabus" asks instructors to state AI expectations in the syllabus, P09.
units.anchor: These policies should be clearly defined in the course syllabus

units.why: "absent a clear syllabus statement" AI use "shall be treated similarly to assistance from another person or an uncited resource" is a fallback rule for silent syllabi (P06), chosen over P45 because the rule is triggered by silence.
units.anchor: absent a clear syllabus statement use of or consultation with generative AI shall be treated
units.policy: Absent a clear syllabus statement, use of or consultation with generative AI shall be treated similarly to assistance from another person or an uncited resource.
units.fit_note: Fallback is an analogy to human help or uncited sources, not an outright ban.

units.why: Faculty and staff "should be mindful of the security implications of information shared with AI tools" in clinical or administrative work, a data-protection duty, P50.
units.anchor: faculty and staff should be mindful of the security implications of information shared with AI

units.why: Entering confidential information into the public ChatGPT interface "is not in compliance with UTMB or UT System policies", a data-protection rule, P50.
units.anchor: entering such information into the public ChatGPT web interface is not in compliance with UTMB

units.why: The sentence names the offices that produced the advisory (Legal Affairs, Compliance, Information Security, Information Services), describing who made the guidance, P84.
units.anchor: produced by UTMB Department of Legal Affairs, The UTMB Office of Institutional Compliance, Information Security

units.why: "Additional guidance will be forthcoming as circumstances and technologies evolve" signals the guidance will be updated, P54.
units.anchor: Additional guidance will be forthcoming as circumstances and technologies evolve

units.why: Public or published university data "can be used freely in AI Tools", a permission within the data-protection rule, so P50 rather than a general permit stance.
units.anchor: can be used freely in AI Tools
units.policy: Data that is publicly available or defined as Published university information can be used freely in AI Tools.

units.why: "In all cases, use should be consistent with the Acceptable Use Policy" ties AI use to an existing university policy, P77.
units.anchor: use should be consistent with the Acceptable Use Policy

units.why: AI tools "cannot use any personal, confidential, proprietary, or otherwise sensitive information" without a protective university contract, a data-protection prohibition, P50.
units.anchor: cannot use any personal, confidential, proprietary, or otherwise sensitive information unless a university contract is
units.fit_note: Exception where a university contract protects the data (vetted tools).

units.why: FERPA student records, health information and Confidential or Controlled data "must not be used with AI Tools", naming data classes; P50.
units.anchor: must not be used with AI Tools
units.policy: Student records subject to FERPA, health information, proprietary information, and any other information classified as Confidential or Controlled data must not be used with AI Tools.

units.why: Among outputs that must not be generated is "completion of academic work in a manner not allowed by the instructor", binding AI use to the instructor's rule; closest is P19, though it defers to the instructor rather than banning outright.
units.anchor: completion of academic work in a manner not allowed by the instructor
units.policy: AI Tools must not be used to generate output that would be considered non-public, for example completion of academic work in a manner not allowed by the instructor.
units.fit_note: The ban depends on what the instructor allows; it is framed as non-public output.

units.why: The same list names "grading" among uses AI "must not be used" for; closest is P46 (humans assign grades), though the text frames it as non-public output.
units.anchor: creation of non-public instructional materials; and grading
units.policy: AI Tools must not be used to generate non-public output such as creation of non-public instructional materials and grading.
units.fit_note: Grading is banned together with creating non-public instructional materials, under a non-public-output rationale; the materials item (P59) is not coded separately.

units.why: "recruitment, personnel, or disciplinary decision making" is listed as output AI must not generate, a limit on AI-based decisions about people, P73.
units.anchor: recruitment, personnel, or disciplinary decision making
units.policy: AI Tools must not be used to generate non-public output such as recruitment, personnel, or disciplinary decision making.
units.fit_note: Bans AI generating such decisions; does not state a human-review requirement.

units.why: "generating proprietary or unpublished research" is listed as prohibited output, an AI rule for research and scholarship, P62.
units.anchor: generating proprietary or unpublished research
units.policy: AI Tools must not be used to generate non-public output such as proprietary or unpublished research.

units.why: Users are asked to "review the usage policies pertaining to all applicable generative AI models", i.e. read vendor terms of use, so P52 (terms of use).
units.anchor: review the usage policies pertaining to all applicable generative AI models
units.fit_note: Concerns vendor usage policies generally, not only copyright or ownership.

units.why: "may not be used for any activity that would be illegal, fraudulent or a violation of any state or federal law, or UTMB or UT System policies" is a rule to follow law and policy (P77); P74 was not chosen because the rule is general compliance. The sentence repeats in the student section and is coded once.
units.anchor: may not be used for any activity that would be illegal, fraudulent or a violation

units.why: "No UTMB Agreement, No Privacy and Security Terms" explains that content entered is "available to ChatGPT, its parent company, OpenAI" and no agreement protects data; a privacy rationale, P50.
units.anchor: All content entered into, or generated by, ChatGPT is available to ChatGPT, its parent company

units.why: The text says no agreement protects data for tools "outside of those constructed within UTMB's contracted Microsoft Azure environments", implying only vetted environments are safe; it only reports the contract gap, so P50 rather than P65 or P92.
units.anchor: any other generative AI tool outside of those constructed within UTMB’s contracted Microsoft Azure environments
units.fit_note: Identifies contracted Azure-built tools as the only ones with agreements (vetted-tool preference).

units.why: "Click-through agreements ... are contracts" and individuals "may face personal consequences" explains personal liability for AI terms of use, P52 (terms of use).
units.anchor: Individuals who accept click-through agreements without delegated signature authority may face personal consequences
units.fit_note: About contractual liability for terms of use, not copyright or ownership.

units.why: The student section says students "may not enter data classified as confidential" into public AI tools, a student-addressed data-protection rule, P50 (P49 is narrower: course materials).
units.anchor: Students may not enter data classified as confidential
units.policy: Students may not enter data classified as confidential, including non-public research data, student records subject to FERPA, health information, proprietary information, and any other information classified as Confidential or Controlled university data into publicly available generative AI Tools.

units.why: "Students may use data that is publicly available or defined as Published university information" permits student use of public data in AI tools, a data rule, P50.
units.anchor: Students may use data that is publicly available or defined as Published university information

units.why: "Students are responsible for any content that they produce or publish that includes AI-generated material" puts ownership on students, P29.
units.anchor: Students are responsible for any content that they produce or publish that includes AI-generated material

units.why: Students "must review all AI-generated content very carefully" because it can be inaccurate or fabricated, a verify-output rule, P31.
units.anchor: Students must review all AI-generated content very carefully

units.why: The warning that AI content "may contain copyrighted material" flags copyright risk in output, P52.
units.anchor: may contain copyrighted material

units.why: Students "clearly indicate the contributions of AI-generated content in accordance with academic citation guidelines": a disclosure requirement, P24.
units.anchor: clearly indicate the contributions of AI-generated content in accordance with academic citation guidelines

units.why: "Failure to do so would be considered a violation of the Student Conduct and Discipline Policy" makes nondisclosure itself the violation, P28 (P36 fits too but the hinge is nondisclosure).
units.anchor: Failure to do so would be considered a violation of the Student Conduct and Discipline

units.why: Violations "may result in disciplinary action ... including academic sanctions, probation, suspension, or expulsion" states possible penalties in advance, P37, though no specific penalty is tied to an offense.
units.anchor: may result in disciplinary action in accordance with university policies
units.fit_note: Lists a range of possible sanctions, not specific penalties per offense.

units.why: "This policy shall be periodically reviewed and updated" commits to review cycles, P54.
units.anchor: This policy shall be periodically reviewed and updated as necessary

notes: Student-section repeats of the non-public-output sentence, the Acceptable Use Policy sentence and the illegal/fraudulent sentence were coded once. Web page chrome skipped. No school or computing documents found.
